headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files, clipboard, and use MCP; Superset exposes an API and allowlisted egress. Cursor’s shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem means content from one can reach the other through files, so injected instructions in shared artifacts are plausible. Superset has no explicit parser hardening shown, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through a shared workspace or exported file, injected instructions can traverse the pair.
IF Superset ingests text from Cursor-produced artifacts without sanitization, instruction hijacking becomes feasible.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents.
Use a read-only handoff file format with strict schema validation.
Strip prompts and comments from any files passed between agents.
Require human review before Superset consumes Cursor-generated text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and has broad network egress plus model-provider calls. Superset’s allowlisted egress means data can leave the local boundary once it receives shared files or API inputs. The pair therefore can leak sensitive workspace data through normal use, even though Superset itself does not list sensitive classes.
conditions: IF Cursor opens files containing secrets or proprietary code and forwards them into model-provider calls, those contents can leave the workstation.
IF Superset receives those artifacts through its API or allowlisted outbound paths, the data can be exposed beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Turn off clipboard sharing between tools.
Use separate service accounts and API keys.
Restrict Cursor to a sanitized project copy.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on files handed from Cursor to Superset.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, git-state modification, and broad egress; Superset can also make outbound API calls. Because Cursor’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via local filesystem, both agents can mutate the same project artifacts without any locking shown. That creates a direct write/write conflict with possible irreversible repo corruption or bad deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can race.
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode while Superset updates shared artifacts, git or file corruption can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches or copies.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Disable Yolo mode for shared repos.
Use file locks around shared outputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, edits, and shell actions; Superset can consume API inputs and act on analytics workflows. If Superset treats Cursor-produced files or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade from a mistaken edit into downstream analytics or operational actions. No verification or provenance controls are shown, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Superset uses Cursor-generated outputs as inputs without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Cursor’s shell or file edits are later operationalized by Superset workflows, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a validation step before Superset consumes Cursor output.
Compare generated artifacts against source-of-truth data.
Limit Superset to read-only analysis on Cursor outputs.
Add checksum checks on exchanged files.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware workflow gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and handles clipboard/open-file content with model-provider egress, while Superset is open-source with allowlisted egress and no sensitive classes listed. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident from differing logging/egress behaviors. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cursor’s open files or clipboard and then sent onward, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Superset is used for the same regulated dataset under a stricter residency policy, the pair may violate internal policy.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Document the data flow between the tools.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated work.
Review retention settings before exchanging artifacts.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end.
